results.evidence_text: High intake of oatmeal in adolescence (≥5 vs. ≤4 times/week) was not significantly associated with risk of PCa diagnosis (OR = 0.99, 95 % CI: 0.77-1.27)
results.one_sentence_explanation: The abstract reports a separable oatmeal-specific estimate for prostate cancer diagnosis in an original cohort study, so Claude+Gemini's INCLUDE is supported and ChatGPT's S2-NO-TARGET-ESTIMATE code is not.

results.evidence_text: We used regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and hazard ratios (HRs) for PCa according to whole-grain consumption
results.manual_review_reason: Study reports whole-grain foods (rye bread, oatmeal, whole-wheat bread) separately; abstract gives no aggregate whole-grain estimate, so poolability for a composite exposure needs checking.
results.one_sentence_explanation: The outcome is prostate cancer and whole-grain consumption is the evaluated exposure, so ChatGPT's S2-CANCER-MISMATCH is unsupported and Claude+Gemini's INCLUDE is supported, though only food-specific rather than aggregate estimates appear in the abstract.
